newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-RAIN SAVES PAKISTAN IN GAME AGAINST INDIA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-RAIN SAVES PAKISTAN IN GAME AGAINST INDIA.

text.p: Rain saved Pakistan on Sunday when their Asian Cup match against India had to be abandoned as a no-result after nine overs at the Singhalese Sports Club.
India won the toss and put their arch rivals into bat under heavy skies and by the time rain stopped play early in the afternoon Pakistan were reeling at 30 for 5.

Indian fast bowler Venkatash Prasad made full use of the conditions to snap up four wickets for just 17 runs in five overs. His new ball partner Abey Kuruvila picked up the other wicket, trapping Pakistan's skipper Rameez Raja for five.
Prasad struck in the first over of the innings by having Saeed Anwar leg before wicket for a duck. Prasad also removed Anwar's opening partner Aamir Sohail, trapping him leg before for one.
Two balls later, Inzamam-ul-Haq, playing forward, edged a catch to Rahul Dravid at gully. The fielder plucked the ball from the air diving to his right.
Shortly afterwards, the light worsened and Pakistan went in placed at 19 for 3 in five overs.
When play resumed after two hours, and the overs reduced to 33 a side, only a further four overs could be delivered before the umpires called it a day.
The match was due to be replayed on Monday at the same venue. The winners play Sri Lanka in the final on July 27.
